web.title: WA Government public holiday review
web.description:
# Public holiday review
The WA Government held a four-week public consultation process from 13 July – 8 August 2025 on proposed changes to the State’s public holiday schedule.

## Proposed changes to WA’s public holiday schedule
- Moving Labour Day to the second Monday in March (currently the first Monday in March). During most State Election years, Labour Day will move to the third Monday in March, to avoid holding an election on a long weekend.
- Moving WA Day to the second Monday in November (currently the first Monday in June).
- Moving the King’s Birthday public holiday to the second Monday in June (currently end of September / early October).
- Recognising Easter Saturday as a public holiday.
- Introduce a new public holiday, Show Day, to be appointed by proclamation to coincide with the first Monday of the September/October school holidays.

These changes aim to better align WA’s public holidays with the rest of the country, support economic activity and productivity, and celebrate Western Australia’s spirit, diverse culture and community achievements.

web.description:
Western Australia will gain two more public holidays in 2028.

New laws will introduce Show Day and Easter Saturday as public holidays for [Western Australian residents,](https://au.news.yahoo.com/fifo-workers-1-million-lotto-win-after-last-minute-change-couldnt-believe-it-000753030.html) while the dates of some other public holidays will be moved.

Labour Day will move from the first Monday in March to the second Monday, falling on March 13 in 2028, while the King's Birthday will go from late September to the second Monday in June, on the 12th.

As Anzac Day - April 25 - falls on the weekend this year and next, Mr Minns believes adding an extra Monday public holiday is very “important”.

WA Day will move to November. Show Day will be held on Monday, September 25 in 2028.

Western Australia will have 13 public holidays in 2028. In years when New Year's Day, Australia Day, Anzac Day, Christmas Day or Boxing Day fall on a Saturday or Sunday extra public holidays will be granted to give WA residents long weekends.

Two years will now be given for businesses, organisations, governments and the broader WA community to prepare for the new 2028 public holiday calendar.

## WA 2028 Public Holidays
New Year's Day: January 1

Australia Day: January 26

Labour Day: March 13

Good Friday: April 14

Easter Saturday: April 15

Easter Sunday: April 16

Easter Monday: April 17

web.title: Public Holiday Review in Western Australia
web.description:
# Public Holiday Review in Western Australia
Aimed at ensuring Western Australia’s public holidays remain relevant, support economic activity and reflect the State’s cultural identity, the reforms would realign several holidays, introduce two new observances and bring the calendar closer to national arrangements. If passed, the changes will affect public holiday entitlements, rostering and payroll planning ahead of an anticipated commencement date in 2028.

#### **Proposed Changes to the Public Holiday Schedule**
- Labour Day to move to the second Monday in March instead of the first Monday in March. In most State Election years, Labour Day would shift to the third Monday in March to avoid elections being held on a long weekend
- WA Day to move to the second Monday in November instead of the first Monday in June
- The King’s Birthday public holiday to move to the second Monday in June instead of the current late September or early October date
- Easter Saturday to become a recognised public holiday, replacing the additional weekday holiday currently provided
- A new public holiday, Show Day, to be appointed by proclamation and aligned with the first Monday of the September or October school holidays
